transcript: So that one line is actually kind of major, and I'm gonna tell you why. Because if you don't know that line, get your phones out, because you're gonna Wanna record. This has not been in the Broadway production since it opened, despite appearing in every other international version of the show. And that is because traditionally, Broadway has not let you record the megasix. This is largely due to just union restrictions. But now, five years into Six's run on Broadway, they have reversed course on that. You are now allowed to legally record the megasix and, in fact, encouraged to do so. Which also totally makes sense given the current cast. You have Dylan Mulvaney and Abigail Barlow, both of whom got very popular off of social media. So allowing their fans to come and film this part of the show, post it online, it becomes free marketing. And in fact, you have probably already seen an onslaught of videos from their first performance already posted. So I'm really not sure what made the unions change their mind and finally say, yes, okay, you can record. But I really do think this could be the thing that reignites Six's popularity in the US. And I am really glad to see them change course on this.
classificationReason: Discusses news about SIX reversing its policy against recording the megasix after 5 years on Broadway. Focuses on casting news (Dylan Mulvaney, Abigail Barlow) and implications for the show's popularity — no first-hand review of attending the production.
